Subject: Developing a cost-effective network shipping plan to meet demand
Date: [Insert Date]

Situation
Our network must move finished goods from multiple source locations to a broad set of destination points. Maintaining on-time availability while keeping freight spend in check is essential for customer satisfaction, margin protection, and budget discipline. Shipping rates vary by lane, and lead-time commitments require us to allocate inventory carefully across the network.

Problem
We need a single, consolidated shipping plan that routes product from each source to the destinations it can serve at the lowest overall cost, without exceeding available inventory at any source and while fully covering the required quantities at every destination. Shipments will be planned in whole units only (no partial loads), so the plan must account for full-unit rounding when balancing supply and demand.

In practical terms:
- Each source can only ship up to its available inventory or capacity within the planning window.
- Each destination must receive its full required quantity within the plan.
- Per-lane shipping costs differ, so the plan should favor lower-cost routes when they can meet the needs without creating shortages elsewhere.
- Where multiple sources can serve the same destination, we will determine the mix that delivers the lowest total landed cost while honoring source limits and whole-unit shipment requirements.

Next steps
- Confirm inventory availability at each source and required quantities at each destination.
- Validate per-lane shipping costs and any accessorials or restrictions that affect feasible routes.
- Build and review a baseline shipping plan that meets all requirements at the lowest total cost, highlighting any trade-offs or service risks.
- Align with Operations and Finance on the recommended plan and contingency options for demand or supply changes.
